newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy March PSBR seen around 14 trln lire.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy March PSBR seen around 14 trln lire.

text.p: Italy's March public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) will not continue the exceptional narrowing trend seen in the first two months of this year, but is still likely to be lower than during the same month last year, a Reuter poll showed.
The PSBR in January and February was around 6.5 trillion lire compared with 25.71 for the same two-month period of 1996.
Analysts surveyed saw on average a requirement of some 14 trillion lire in March against 18.84 trillion in March 1996.
"This month will be a bit better than a year ago but we won't again see the positive factors in the first two months," said Davide Tesoro of Banque Indosuez.
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore speculated this week that the March PSBR figure could be around 15 trillion lire.
If March PSBR came in at 14 to 15 trillion lire, then the first quarter deficit would be between 20.5 and 21.5 trillion lire against 44.1 trillion a year ago.

Hugo Doyle of Banca Commerciale Italiana said March would see the first effects of the government's Eurotax -- a one off levy on income tax aimed to raise some 5.5 trillion lire over the period March to November this year.
"March will be better thanks to savings on interest charges, estimated at 1.0 trillion lire per month for the whole of this year, as well as the Eurotax," said Andrea Marchetti of Credito Italiano.

"The March data will be useful in order to see the trend after January and February....(and) the effects of accounting adjustments and expenditure carried out in 1996 instead of at the start of the year," said Bruno Rovelli of Bank of America.

"As for the trend of PSBR in coming months, the most important factors will be the amount of the corrective mini-budget, the amount of future tax payments, the extent of economic growth and the amount of local authorities' drawings on Treasury accounts," said Davide Tesoro.

Following are the analysts' forecasts (in trillion lire). The figures, apart from those of Bank of America and Banca di Roma forecasts, do not take into account of the effects of a possible supplementary mini-budget.
March PSBR 1997 PSBR
Bank of America 15.5 65.0
J.P.Morgan 13.5 77.0
Chase Manhattan Bank 13.0 73.0

Credito Italiano 13.0 71.5
Banca di Roma 15.0 75.0
Banque Indosuez 15.0 72/74.0
CONSENSUS 14.0 73.0
